title: An icon picture's SVG reads in 24 whole units
goal: An icon drawn in a 512 picture exports with long fractions, because 24 units do not divide into 512. A person handing the file to a developer expects a 24 by 24 icon with whole numbers, the way an icon frame already writes it.
notes: From the rough list of queue/audits/2026-11-04-ask-makes-icons-that-are-icons.json: 'The numbers in an icon's SVG are fractions, because a 24 grid does not divide into 512.' Objective icon-export: whole-unit coordinates. An icon frame already writes whole units (m5.json: 'M18 6 C18 9.314 ...'). Decided here: keep the 512 canvas, which is what the user's task named, and let one unit be 512 / 24 in the picture; only the SVG writes in units. App Icon stays 1024 with its own numbers. Waits for the task that marks a document as an icon, since that mark says which pictures write this way.
acceptance: An icon drawn on whole units in a File, New, Image, Icon picture exports as SVG with viewBox 0 0 24 24 and every point on a whole unit, except where a curve's own handles need a fraction
An icon Ask made exports the same way, and Copy puts that same SVG on the clipboard
The drawing looks the same at every size as before: a rendered comparison of the 512 canvas and the exported file differs by no visible amount
PNG export of the same picture still comes out at 512 unless the sheet says otherwise

Try path: File, New, Image, Icon, draw with the Pen, Export as SVG, read the file. Audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not
